title: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013
description: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) headquarters in Tokyo, Japan, on Friday, Dec. 19, 2025. Photographer: Akio Kon/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg
body: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) headquarters in Tokyo, Japan, on Friday, Dec. 19, 2025. Photographer: Akio Kon/Bloomberg via Getty ImagesBloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesThe Bank of Japan declared that underlying inflation in the country was "generally consistent" with its target of 2%, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.Before this, the BOJ used to say that underlying inflation has been "approaching 2 percent."This comes as the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995.The decision was split 8-1, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting. Takata had wanted the bank to hike its policy rate to 1.5%. The BOJ also upgraded its inflation forecast for its fiscal year 2027 to 2.6% from 2.4%, with the so-called "core-core" inflation forecast also raised to 2.7% from 2.6%. The "core-core" inflation strips out prices of fresh food and energy. It also flagged a risk that underlying inflation will deviate upward beyond 2%, saying that "firms' behavior has been shifting more toward raising wages and prices and there are various factors that could drive up prices."A CNBC survey of 16 economists before the decision revealed that all surveyed expect the BOJ to set the stage for a rate hike in December or January next year, as domestic inflation and wages continue to rise.Thirteen respondents said they expect a terminal rate, or the level at which the BOJ is expected to stop its tightening cycle, of 1.75% to 2% by around mid-2027.Japan has been grappling with a weak yen and high energy prices that have pushed up inflation. However, experts have told CNBC that CPI numbers are being held down by energy subsidies from the Takaichi administration. The most recent inflation numbers for September revealed core inflation hit their highest level in 2026, coming in at 2.1% and overshooting expectations. Earlier this month, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reportedly told parliament that Japan was "on the cusp of shifting to a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages."Japan's inflation-adjusted wages rose for the eighth month in a row in August, climbing 1.5% from a year earlier, according to the most recent government data, signaling potential wage-growth-driven inflation as well.— CNBC's Lisa Kim contributed to this report.  This is breaking news, please check back for updates.

schema.headline: BOJ holds rates as underlying inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013

title: Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout
description: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Im
body: Circle signage during the company's initial public offering in front of the New York Stock Exchange, June 5, 2025.Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesBinance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses.The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe.Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds.The company said it would publish a technical report, and an updated Proof of Reserves after remediation efforts."We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified," Binance said.The announcement followed moves by several crypto firms, including Circle Internet Group, Tether and Ripple, to freeze funds tied to the hack.Bitcoin fell more than 4% to $77,994.96 on Friday as the hack weighed on crypto markets. Shares of Circle tumbled about 5% in after-hours trading on Thursday. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Binance also said on X that Binance Alpha trading had been temporarily suspended, and that "the current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion."Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening in a social media post that the company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with the incident. USDT stablecoin issuer Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino also said in on X that his firm had frozen more than 1.5 billion of its stablecoin that may have been related to a potential breach. Jack McDonald, Ripple's senior vice president of stablecoins, said it was actively freezing affected funds held in RLUSD, its U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin. Later, Binance co-founder Yi He said in a statement that the XRP and RLUSD-tied firm Ripple helped halt the movement of $200 million of funds linked to the possible attack.  But those frozen funds could represent only part of those impacted. Crypto data provider Arkham Intelligence linked nearly $6 billion in digital assets — including bitcoin, ether, solana and various stablecoins — to 55 wallet addresses it has linked to the potential exploit.Arkham identifies, tracks and flags crypto wallets by analyzing publicly available blockchain data. It also solicits tips from its community members.Exploits are not uncommon in the crypto space. In 2025, Bybit suffered roughly $1.5 billion in losses due to a hack. More recently, Bitget lost more than $350 million worth of digital assets in a cyber theft incident. Over the past several years, bad actors have also drained billions of dollars in crypto from decentralized exchanges.

schema.headline: Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout

title: Norwegian shares surge 13% on earnings beat, guidance raise
description: Norwegian Sky, a 77,104 GT Sun-class cruise ship owned and operated by Norwegian Cruise Line, sails the Tagus River after departure from the cruise te
body: Norwegian Sky, a 77,104 GT Sun-class cruise ship owned and operated by Norwegian Cruise Line, sails the Tagus River after departure from the cruise terminal on Sept. 2, 2025, in Lisbon, Portugal.Horacio Villalobos | Corbis News | Getty ImagesShares of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings surged 13% Thursday after the company posted better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its outlook for the full year. The cruise line reported third-quarter revenue of $2.95 billion, topping Wall Street expectations of $2.88 billion, according to analyst estimates from LSEG. Net income for the period was $491 million, or $1.07 per share.Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was $937 million, which exceeded Norwegian's previous guidance of $874 million. Adjusted EPS was $1.12, exceeding previous guidance of 90 cents and outpacing analysts' expectations of 94 cents, per LSEG. Norwegian also raised its full-year guidance, citing its stronger-than-expected third-quarter performance. The company now expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.55 billion and adjusted EPS of about $1.70. The report said the company's bookings had "improved modestly" since its last report but remain below its optimal range. Norwegian said it will emphasize new marketing strategies, including the launch of a new marketing platform in January. It also said it anticipates that enhancements such as a new waterpark at its Great Stirrup Cay private island will support stronger demand. Also on Thursday, Norwegian announced that Chief Financial Officer Mark Kempa will step down after more than 25 years at the company. Meghan Montana, currently chief strategy officer, will take over the role starting Jan. 1.

schema.headline: Norwegian shares surge 13% on earnings beat, guidance raise

title: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam
description: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol speaks during the Starbucks Investor Day event in New York City, U.S., Jan. 29, 2026. Brendan McDermid | ReutersStarbucks o
body: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol speaks during the Starbucks Investor Day event in New York City, U.S., Jan. 29, 2026. Brendan McDermid | ReutersStarbucks on Thursday reported mixed quarterly results as its international cafes underperformed expectations.However, its U.S. turnaround continues to take hold, as its home market topped expectations during the coffee giant's final quarter of fiscal 2026. "We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared on the company's website.Starbucks is ahead of schedule to meet the fiscal 2028 targets laid out at its investor day in January, he said on the company's earnings conference call.For fiscal 2027, Starbucks is projecting adjusted earnings per share in a range of $3.15 to $3.25, above Wall Street's expectations of earnings per share of $3.14. However, its anticipated revenue decline of 1% is weaker than expected; analysts were forecasting net sales growth of 1.4%. Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year. The company's earnings and revenue outlook includes an additional week and the effects of the shift in its China business to a joint venture business model. Starbucks is also projecting slight deflation in coffee prices and slowing net new North American cafe openings, which will both weigh on its full-year revenue, according to CFO Cathy Smith.Shares of Starbucks fell nearly 2% in extended trading.Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Sept. 27 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:Earnings per share: 80 cents adjusted vs. 72 cents expectedRevenue: $9.14 billion vs. $9.23 billion expectedStarbucks reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income attributable to the company of $677.2 million, or 59 cents per share, up from $133.1 million, or 12 cents per share, a year earlier.Excluding restructuring and impairment costs and other items, the company reported earnings per share of 80 cents.Net revenue fell 4% to $9.14 billion, reflecting the joint venture deal in China.The company's global same-store sales increased 7.2%, fueled by growth in average ticket, and beating Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount. Transactions grew 1.8% in the quarter.Starbucks' U.S. cafes reported same-store sales growth of 7.7%, topping StreetAccount estimates of a 6.5% increase.Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service, making its cafes more welcoming and sharpening its marketing. The changes have helped to win back customers."Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses," Niccol told analysts.The company said its North American rollout of its fall menu, which includes the iconic pumpkin spice latte, was the company's strongest ever autumn launch day. And matcha is now a $1 billion drink for Starbucks.Outside of North America, the company's international comparable sales ticked up 0.9%, as traffic declines offset an increase to average ticket. That growth fell short of analyst estimates of a 3.2% increase, according to StreetAccount.After its China business transitioned to a joint venture, Starbucks has shifted most of its international business to a licensed model, allowing local operators to take charge. The company is also exploring selling a majority stake in its Japan business, Reuters reported in September.Starbucks opened 303 net new cafes during the quarter. In September, the company announced it would close about 1% of its North American footprint, or about 250 locations, as part of its turnaround.By the end of its fiscal year, across the U.S. and Canada, the company also completed more than 1,700 cafe uplifts, meant to make its stores more welcoming to customers. The company has said locations that receive a makeover, with tweaks like increased seating and softer lighting, see higher transactions in the aftermath.

schema.headline: Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam

title: Alphabet tanks nearly 13% for worst day ever, losing $500 billion in value
description: watch nowAlphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap. I
body: watch nowAlphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap. In its earnings announcement late Wednesday, Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, compared to the $2.7 billion analysts expected. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.Microsoft, meanwhile, traded largely flat as investors focused on the tech giants' latest spending and free cash flow numbers in the third-quarter earnings report.Microsoft reported $45.2 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases during the quarter, which was 30% higher than a year ago, but below analyst projections of $50.67 billion. Free cash flow fell 27% to $18.63 billion but remained positive.The earnings reports come as investors scrutinize AI spending plans of tech companies and are focusing on the returns on those investments. "Microsoft is building out its architecture in a measured way and as such contains fewer surprises," Ben Barringer, global head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said on Thursday. "Alphabet, by contrast, saw its share price hit after hours as a result of a fairly messy set of results and a poorly handled earnings call" .Read more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optionalSearch under pressureAlphabet's biggest source of revenue, search advertising, grew 12% in the September quarter to $63.35 billion, but missed analyst expectations, adding further pressure to the company's shares.Philipp Schindler, Alphabet's chief business officer, said the impact on the search business was partly because of lower monetization within the company's AI Mode. He added that Alphabet is now "scaling" ads within its AI Overviews and AI Mode products, including in international markets. Google's search business has faced headwinds from the rise of other AI chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. People may be carrying out more search queries outside Google. Gemini, Google's own AI chatbot, has failed to keep pace."The problem for Google is it faces an innovator's dilemma and doesn't know whether to protect its core business or look to join the disruption. As such, Google has lost its edge with Gemini and is behind peers on agentic AI," Barringer said.Google's dominant market share in the search business, however, could ultimately give it a leg up over its peers, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Scott Devitt said. "I don't think it's a sea change," Devitt told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Thursday. "If it's a problem for Alphabet, it's a problem for any consumer-facing AI agent or LLM as well. And so, it's a problem that I think is ultimately going to be resolved. And when it does, Alphabet, with its 4 billion search customers that become AI customers, is in an enviable position."- CNBC's Robert Hum, Samantha Subin, Jordan Novet and Caleigh Keating contributed reporting.

schema.headline: Alphabet tanks nearly 13% for worst day ever, losing $500 billion in value

title: ServiceNow shares plunge 27% to worst day ever after earnings revive AI disruption fears
description: Bill McDermott, CEO of ServiceNow speaks with CNBC on May 5, 2026.CNBCServiceNow shares sank 27% on Thursday and recorded their worst day on record af
body: Bill McDermott, CEO of ServiceNow speaks with CNBC on May 5, 2026.CNBCServiceNow shares sank 27% on Thursday and recorded their worst day on record after the enterprise software company's third-quarter results underwhelmed, reigniting artificial intelligence disruption concerns."This was a little bit uncharacteristic for ServiceNow standards, just in terms of the lack of upside," Citi's Tyler Radke told CNBC on Thursday.Revenue grew more than 20% during the period to $4.11 billion, which was roughly in line with a $4.10 billion estimate from analysts polled by LSEG. Adjusted earnings came up short at $1.00 per share, compared to a forecast of $1.02.The results did little to overturn recent "SaaSpocalypse" fears, or concerns that new AI capabilities will upend traditional software business models.The stock drop came even after the company slightly lifted its full-year 2026 subscription revenue outlook to between $15.78 billion and $15.79 billion. Net new AI average contract value jumped 65%. One factor spooking investors is the lack of immediate payoff for the company's investments in its newly formed forward-deployed engineering team that embeds in enterprises to build AI solutions, Radke said. "It's just going to be a little bit longer of a waiting game, and so I think the market, you know, wanted to see something a little bit sooner," he said. "I think you got to wait until next year to really see that inflection."WATCH: ServiceNow shares plummet in extended trading on mixed Q3 resultswatch nowRead more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optional

title: Nvidia responds to report Jensen Huang was target of Chinese asset, says diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'
description: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, presents new NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX Pod Full-Stack Modular AI Factory as he gives a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Tech
body: Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA, presents new NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX Pod Full-Stack Modular AI Factory as he gives a keynote address at the Berlin GPU Technology Conference (GTC) on October 21, 2026 in Berlin, Germany.Sean Gallup | Getty ImagesAn Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset.According to the Times report, which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump. The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information. The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China.Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. "The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement. Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said. Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China. Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology.As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure. Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China. Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed. "Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.

schema.headline: Nvidia responds to report Jensen Huang was target of Chinese asset, says diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'

title: Israel faces weeks of coalition haggling as Netanyahu’s party claims election 'stolen'
description: (COMBO) This combination of pictures created on October 28, 2026, showsYashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot (L) addressing his supporters at the election
body: (COMBO) This combination of pictures created on October 28, 2026, showsYashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot (L) addressing his supporters at the election night rally in Tel Aviv early on October 28, 2026, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaking to the media after voting in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026.Maya Levin, jewel Samad | Afp | Getty ImagesIsrael’s final election count left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc and the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.The outcome sets up weeks of coalition bargaining and political uncertainty, with the opposition alliance facing an uphill battle to assemble a majority government in the 120-seat Knesset.Netanyahu’s Likud party and its hard-right allies won 53 seats in the Knesset, according to the Central Elections Committee, short of the 61 needed for a majority and down from 64 seats in the 2022 election.The main opposition bloc, led by Eisenkot, won 48 seats, falling short of the 61 needed for a majority.  Eisenkot now faces a difficult coalition path. Most parties in his bloc have rejected relying on the Arab-led parties, while Eisenkot has said neither meets his conditions for a partnership. The Joint List and Ra’am won a combined 19 seats, an all-time high for Arab-led parties.Netanyahu's party has intensified claims that the Arab-led parties "stole" the election, amplifying an allegation that spread after exit polls showed the prime minister's bloc had suffered a setback.Likud asserted Thursday, without evidence, that foreign interference was "aimed at facilitating a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel and toppling of the right wing government."The statement came a day after Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, who chairs the Central Elections Committee, asked the Shin Bet security agency to investigate "serious suspicions" of improper influence through funding from foreign entities. Sohlberg said he couldn't attest to the substance of the suspicions and directed agencies to verify the claims.Qatar, accused of trying to mobilize Arab voters, has denied interfering in the elections, calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.”Opposition leaders also called for a full investigation, while warning against using the allegations to cast doubt on or otherwise influence the election results.watch nowAlthough the vote count is complete, the results remain subject to possible “minor corrections” before they are certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog next Wednesday, according to the Central Elections Committee.The new Knesset is due to be sworn in Nov. 10, while parties have until Nov. 18 to challenge the results. 'Comeback kid'A prolonged political stalemate could leave Netanyahu in office as caretaker prime minister through another round of coalition negotiations or potentially another election. A return to war with Iran also remains a key risk."Bibi [Netanyahu] is known as a 'comeback kid.' He did not become the longest-serving prime minister by accident," said P R Kumaraswamy, emeritus professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, adding that he expected Netanyahu to maintain his current approach on Iran and Gaza for now.Israeli assets have come under pressure this week with the shekel sustaining the worst intraday decline since 2023 on Wednesday before regaining ground. Tel Aviv's key benchmark stock index dropped 4.1% for the week as of Friday morning, according to LSEG data. "We expect some near-term volatility for Israeli assets until a new government is formed and decides on fiscal consolidation and war-related spending," said Eirini Tsekeridou, a fixed-income analyst at Julius Baer. She added that Israel's economic fundamentals and monetary policy should provide support. What happens next?President Herzog will begin consulting with the competing parties next week and name the leader he believes has the best chance of forming a majority government. Netanyahu may get the first call to kick off the 28-day process to build a coalition that can be extended by up to 14 day. If those efforts fail, new elections will be called with Netanyahu remaining in office in the interim. The previous government-formation efforts have taken between 20 and 100 days, according to the Israel Democracy Institute.Netanyahu could also push for a national unity government, arguing that the country should come together as it faces conflict on several fronts, though many of his opponents have ruled out such an arrangement.

schema.headline: Israel faces weeks of coalition haggling as Netanyahu’s party claims election 'stolen'

title: Amazon AWS posts 39% revenue growth as cloud rivals also accelerate
description: Visitors crowd the Amazon Web Services (AWS) exhibition stand at the 2026 Hannover Messe industrial trade fair on April 20, 2026 in Hanover, Germany.S
body: Visitors crowd the Amazon Web Services (AWS) exhibition stand at the 2026 Hannover Messe industrial trade fair on April 20, 2026 in Hanover, Germany.Sean Gallup | Getty ImagesAmazon's cloud-computing unit reported more rapid third-quarter growth than analysts had projected.Revenue came in at $45.98 billion, up 39% year over year and above the $45.29 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount, according to a statement. Growth in the second quarter came in at about 37%."Our core compute and storage revenue grew at their fastest rates in several years," Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with analysts. The AWS growth rate was the highest since the fourth quarter of 2021.Amazon remains the top cloud by revenue, but growth has also sped up at rivals Alphabet and Microsoft. On Wednesday Alphabet said the Google Cloud business, which contains infrastructure and Google Workspace subscriptions, more than doubled in the third quarter.All the major clouds have been racing to build data centers that can accommodate high artificial intelligence demand. During the quarter, AWS announced plans to expand its portfolio of Nvidia graphics processing units that can handle AI workloads.AWS also acquired data analysis startup DuckLabs and signed deals with Meta and OpenAI, according to the statement.The AWS segment generated $17.77 billion in third-quarter operating income, up 55% and more than the $16.97 billion StreetAccount consensus.The unit now accounts for almost 23% of Amazon's revenue, a record.On Wednesday, Microsoft published its first earnings report that contained revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars. Azure is 72% the size of AWS, up from 58% two years ago.AWS came before Azure and the Google Cloud Platform, with its first services appearing in 2006."With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we're adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years," Jassy said.Google has been pumping up its cloud revenue by making its tensor processing units for AI available outside its own facilities. Now Amazon will adopt the strategy with its Trainium chips for training models, starting in late 2027."With Trainium demand so strong, customers continue encouraging us to make it available outside of AWS. We intend to do so late in 2027," Jassy said. WATCH: Big Tech earnings put AI spending and profitability in focus: Analystwatch now

title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
description: Steve Huffman, co-founder and CEO of Reddit, speaks during the WSJ Tech Live conference hosted by The Wall Street Journal at the Montage Laguna Beach
body: Steve Huffman, co-founder and CEO of Reddit, speaks during the WSJ Tech Live conference hosted by The Wall Street Journal at the Montage Laguna Beach in Laguna Beach, California, on Oct. 21, 2024.Frederic J. Brown | Afp | Getty ImagesReddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet." The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released.Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates:Earnings per share: $1.40 vs. $1.35 expectedRevenue: $895 million vs. $878 million expectedReddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to the "shift to AI mode and AI overviews." The traffic decline played a big role in Reddit's planned efforts to require people to become logged-in users. A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic. "I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.  Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now."The CEO didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity. The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.Read more CNBC tech newsAI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecastsAlphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of searchAs Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning businessHands-on with Apple’s first touchscreen laptop: Touch is totally optionalHuffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users, because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads."The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion."It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership."I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet.""Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.WATCH: Rotations in the market are likely to continue.watch now

title: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates
description: watch nowThe pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster
body: watch nowThe pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday.The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below.Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends.While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter.Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%.The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move."The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday.However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do.A Labor Department report also released Thursday showed that layoffs remain low. Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 24, below the estimate for 200,000 and near levels last seen in the late 1960s.Stock market futures were negative following the releases while Treasury yields also fell."Net, net, economic growth is powering ahead despite the uncertainty of geopolitical risks and the damage posed to many sectors of the economy by higher energy costs," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. "The economy was thought to have been a lost cause during much of the current Administration's time in office, but real GDP has bounced back above a 3 percent run rate in Q3 2026 for the first time in a year."Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products.Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter.There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter.September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%.At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

schema.headline: Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates

title: IRS CEO Bisignano donates to Trump Accounts in his childhood Brooklyn ZIP code
description: Frank Bisignano, CEO of the Internal Revenue Service, during a House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Social Security hearing in Washington, June 10, 20
body: Frank Bisignano, CEO of the Internal Revenue Service, during a House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Social Security hearing in Washington, June 10, 2026.Tierney L. Cross | Bloomberg | Getty ImagesIRS CEO Frank Bisignano has donated to Trump Accounts for certain kids in Brooklyn, the agency announced Thursday.The Bisignano Family Fund donated $250 apiece to Trump Accounts of eligible children ages 2 to 8 living in 11234, Bisignano's hometown ZIP code, according to the release. "My life was shaped by the people, schools, and neighborhoods in Marine Park, Mill Basin, Bergen Beach, and Flatlands," Bisignano said in a statement. "This donation is an investment in the children of Brooklyn, giving them a boost in their personal wealth building journeys."Within that ZIP code, fewer than 10,000 U.S. citizens are under 10 years of age, according to CNBC's analysis of the most recent population estimate from the U.S. Census Bureau. The contribution will be invested in a diversified index fund, the release also said. Expanding access to Trump Accounts has been a Trump administration priority. In July, Bisignano was tasked with leading that effort. Read more CNBC personal finance coverageIf Elon Musk gifts SpaceX stock through Trump Accounts, it will come with a catchRoth conversions aren't for everyone. When the 'juice' isn't worth it: Top advisorThe affordability crisis isn't hitting all voters equally. Here's whyMidterm elections: How affordability and the economy could affect voters' decisionsCNBC's Financial Advisor 100: Best financial advisors, top firms for 2026 rankedCNBC Elite Advisors: Top ultra-high net worth wealth management firms for 2026The latest Trump Account news comes weeks after the Treasury Department auto-enrolled more than 60 million children.Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. citizen under 18 with a Social Security number. Children born from 2025 through 2028 may also claim a one-time $1,000 pilot program contribution from the Treasury.Families must still activate their child's Trump Account to receive contributions if eligible, according to Treasury guidance.'The tip of the iceberg'Bisignano's commitment comes on the heels of news that Elon Musk plans to give every kid in America a share of SpaceX in 2027.Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, founder of Invest America and an architect of Trump Accounts, described Musk's gift as "the tip of the iceberg" for philanthropic gifts on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Oct. 21. Gerstner has committed about $35 million to help fund investment accounts for kids in his home state of Indiana.       More gifts are in the pipeline, Bisignano told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Oct. 8. "They range from small to mega," he said. After claiming an account, families can track deposits in the Trump Accounts app, which was designed in partnership with Robinhood."Trump Accounts is direct philanthropy, extremely efficient, direct to children...," Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Oct. 28."Excited to see Elon donation," he said. "I think there will be many others as well."watch nowThe Treasury Department in September released temporary regulations allowing Trump Accounts to hold donated individual stocks, a shift from previous guidelines that permitted only diversified, low-cost index funds. The Trump administration said the move could pave the way for more multimillion-dollar donations, with a number of philanthropists poised to participate. The latest donation comes just days before the midterm election, and Republicans fight to keep slim congressional majorities in the Senate and House.

title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
description: The official logo signage is pictured on the exterior facade of a Microsoft Corporation office building in Lehi, Utah, United States, on August 26, 20
body: The official logo signage is pictured on the exterior facade of a Microsoft Corporation office building in Lehi, Utah, United States, on August 26, 2026.Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty ImagesMicrosoft on Thursday announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support its infrastructure expansion. The software maker holds a top-tier AAA rating with S&P, a credit agency. Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients."Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes,  which may include, among other things, funding for working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt," according to a statement. The offerings should close on Nov. 4, the company said. Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint. Investors have turned more skittish on companies with tall debt piles as central bankers raise interest rates to fight inflation.Microsoft will access additional funding sources to complement its own cash flow generation when conditions are attractive, Amy Hood, its finance chief, said on the company's earnings call on Wednesday. "There's a form of financing called leasing, and we've been using that one as a vehicle," she said. "We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our ratings are, and we haven't yet tapped that."Microsoft reported positive free cash flow on Wednesday, differentiating itself from Alphabet, whose cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row. Last week Meta said it had negative free cash flow, and on Thursday Amazon reported negative free cash flow.Also on Wednesday, Oracle unveiled plans to raise $10 billion in new debt and said it anticipates a return to positive free cash flow in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year.WATCH: We need AI token prices to come down, says Citi's Heath Terrywatch now

title: Intel stock plunges 21% as chipmaker blames PC slowdown for weak guidance
description: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | AFP | Getty ImagesIntel shares plumme
body: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | AFP | Getty ImagesIntel shares plummeted more than 20% in extended trading on Thursday after the chipmaker issued a weak fourth-quarter forecast, citing continued softness in the global PC market.Here's how the company did in the third quarter, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG:Earnings per share: 52 cents adjusted vs. 40 cents expectedRevenue: $16.51 billion vs. $16.5 billion expectedRevenue climbed 21% from $13.7 billion a year earlier, the company said in a press release. However, revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion.Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG."We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." Intel's forecast reflects the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said on Thursday's earnings. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips.Intel's stock has been on an upward tear, up about 150% so far this year prior to the earnings report, although it's down roughly 23% in October over growing concern over the size of the artificial intelligence buildout. "We will remain disciplined as we invest, and we will not spend $1 of capital unless we have confidence in the health of our products and process technologies, and clear evidence of customer demand," Zinsner said on the call.Nvidia, which has become the world's most valuable company thanks to its dominance in graphics processing units, or GPUs, is scheduled to report results in mid-November. Advanced Micro Devices, a maker of GPUs and central processing units, or CPUs, reports next week. Known best for its industry-leading CPUs, Intel has been a beneficiary of the rise in agentic AI. While chatbots and large models rely heavily on graphics processors from Nvidia and AMD, agentic applications such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots lean on CPUs to help orchestrate tasks and data from a computer operating in the cloud."Despite near term headwinds affecting the broader PC industry, we continue to see robust demand for CPUs and more broadly, for all our computing platforms in the long term," Tan said in the press release.watch nowIntel's foundry business, meanwhile, has struggled to find its footing.Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Its next fab in Arizona is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028.For now, Intel has no major external customers for its new chips. "We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips.The Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel last year after the company had fallen behind on its 7- and 10-nanometer technologies. Nvidia and Softbank also invested billions in Intel last year.  Tan has taken a more cautious approach to foundry spending than his predecessor, Pat Gelsinger, who launched an ambitious revival of the foundry business. Last week, Intel said crews have installed the first structural truss at its huge Ohio fab that was originally expected to deliver chips in 2025.In September, reports surfaced that the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory, SK Hynix may team up with Intel in Ohio to lease some foundry space to make memory chips at the new site. Neither company would confirm any plans. "We continue to evaluate unique and highly differentiated opportunities to accelerate our Ohio build out, and I hope to share more on this in the near future" Tan said on the call.Intel completed a $23 billion equity offering in August. Tech giants have spent trillions of dollars in recent years to meet insatiable demand for AI and the infrastructure needed to support it.Tan said he's "disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter." title: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
description: U.S. President Donald Trump attends a rally, in support of Republican Senate candidate, former U.S. Representative Mike Rogers, ahead of the midterm e
body: U.S. President Donald Trump attends a rally, in support of Republican Senate candidate, former U.S. Representative Mike Rogers, ahead of the midterm elections, at an entertainment complex in Port Huron, Michigan on Oct. 25, 2026.Jonathan Ernst | ReutersIn August, President Donald Trump claimed that 97% of Republican candidates he backed had won their primary races.And it's true that Trump has shown an ability to influence races particularly in Republican primaries, picking off politicians he didn't like such as Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky. But while he hasn't shied away from expressing his opinions on foreign leaders, his influence over other countries' elections is proving less strong.Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection on Sunday, defeating Trump-aligned Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father Jair had also been a Trump ally. Also last weekend, a student-led movement in Serbia defeated the ruling party of Aleksandar Vucic, a populist leader who had cultivated ties with Trump and his circle. Vucic had served as Serbia's president from 2017, and as prime minister from 2014 to 2017.During his concession speech, Vucic said that the loss was due to a "legitimization of a revolution carried out by the people with direct support from various European countries and the American deep state, the one that opposes President Trump." Earlier this year, Vice President JD Vance had visited Hungary for two days and publicly backed then-Prime Minister Viktor Orban. However, Orban, who is also a staunch ally and endorsed by Trump, lost that election and was ejected from office after 16 years.In October, Trump also endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection. While the results of the Oct. 27 election are not finalized yet, the Associated Press said that Netanhayu's Likud party had appeared to lose its majority in the country's parliament.Still, Trump's influence on any one global election remains variable, experts said."Elections are always national first and regional or global a very distant second," Cas Mudde, professor of international affairs at the University of Georgia, told CNBC. Furthermore, it is also not clear that Trump ever had a great influence over far-right actors elsewhere, said Stijn van Kessel, professor of comparative politics at Queen Mary University of London."Far-right parties and politicians like to celebrate each others' victories as it allows them to portray themselves as part of a successful global movement," he said, adding that those relationships can sour quickly when national interests collide and the foreign partner turns toxic in the eyes of the domestic electorate.Van Kessel pointed to the fallout between Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni earlier this year, which stemmed from Italy's refusal to allow U.S. aircraft to use one of the NATO airbases for its war on Iran. Trump later claimed that Meloni "begged" him for a photo at the G7 summit, a claim that sparked a denial from Meloni. Right wing strengthStill, right-wing movements remain strong in numerous places globally. In France, Marine Le Pen is currently the frontrunner to succeed President Emmanuel Macron, according to a compilation of polls by Politico. However, historically she has often started out leading a crowded field of hopefuls before support consolidates around a more moderate candidate.In Germany, the far-right Alternative fur Deutschland, or AfD party won 20.8% of the vote in the country's February 2025 federal election, making it the country's largest opposition party. Trump ally Javier Milei leads Argentina, and Colombia's new President Abelardo de la Espriella was elected on a far-right platform.Still, Mudde noted that most far-right leaders disassociate themselves from Trump when he becomes more unpopular in their country. Trump's poll numbers remain near a record low even in the U.S. over issues including the Iran war and the cost of living as energy prices soar. "Voters are willing to give anyone a shot when they are economically frustrated, but when those experiments fail, they move on to something else," said David Barker, a professor of government at American University in Washington, D.C. At this point, Trump "undermines his allies' ability to maintain support."

schema.headline: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
